decisions.reason: It is a strongly publicized extension of the firm’s core airfield systems business, so the prior R&D and launch commitment make management likely to continue with it despite any uncertainty.
As a surveillance display tied to the established airport-operations portfolio, it fits the firm’s announced integration strategy and has enough visible commitment behind it to discourage withdrawal.
Training is part of the firm’s service logic and supports the installed base, so even if results are modest management can justify keeping it as a complementary offering.
This narrow training course appears to have involved less investment and less public commitment than the technology products, making it easier for management to discontinue if traction is limited.
Collaboration software is closely aligned with the firm’s stated move toward intelligent, real-time, integrated airport operations, so management is likely to persist with it.
The multilateration surveillance system reflects substantial technical investment and was launched very visibly, which under escalation of commitment makes management especially reluctant to pull it.
